FOREWORD This Icdian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Aircraft Electrical Equipments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IS0 3456 : 1975 `AircraftLever-operated manual switches ( Class 3 ) - Performance requirements' issued by International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). For the purpose of deciding, whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard
AIRCRAFT - PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENT FOR LEVEROPERATED MANUAL SWITCHES ( CLASS 3 ) - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE
1.1 This standard specifies the performance requirements for the single and triple hole lever operated manual switches mounting, ( class 3 ) for use in nominal 28 V dc and 115/200 V three phase 400 Hz ac systems in aircraft.

preferably be designed to allow the incorporation of integral locking of the lever in any or all positions. 3.4 The method of operation of the switch shall b: by means of a single lever, moving in a plane perpendicular to the mounting panel. The relationship of the lever positions to the keyways, and the relationship of the terminal numbers to the lever positions shall be stated in the individual specification. 3.5 The switch terminals shall be identified by number in the sequence shown in the individual specification. 4 DIMENSIONS 4.1 The envelope and fixing dimensions for the switch shall comply with IS 13269 : 1991. 5 OPERATION 5.1 It shall not be possible to rotate the lever about its longitudinal axis, unless otherwise specified in the applicable individual specification. 5.2 The angular movement of the lever shall be in accordance with IS 13269 : 1991 or other applicable individual specification. 5.3 The lever shall be capable of withstanding without damage or distortion a force of 90 N applied steadily in the directions stated in 11.9.2. 5.4 There shall be at least a 4" movement of the lever before switching occurs. 6 CONSTRUCTI~ON 6.1 The lever, including any metal inserts, shall be insulated from all live parts. 6.2 The force required to operate the switch shall be not less than 2'7 N and not more than 45 N. For each operation of a-particular type of switch, the maximum force shall not exceed the minimum force by more than 200 percent. This maximum-to-minimum force value does not apply to spring-return switches. 6.3 Where locking of the lever is provided, it shall be positive and automatic, and the lock shall be released by raising the lever against a spring force of 6'7 to 22 N. 6.4 The exposed portion a non-glaring finish. 1 of the switch shall have

1.2 The switches are ~environmentally sealed and suitable for higher altitude and temperature conditions than are class 2 switches which are sealed only at the lever entry. They do not have the positive action features of the class 1 and class 2 switches as specified in IS 13309 : 1991 `Aircraft-Performance requirements of lever operated manual switches ( class 1 and 2 >Specification'. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this Standard.

3 DESIGN EQUIPMENTS 3.1 The switch shall be suitable for use at altitudes up to 20 000 m and at temperatures within the range - 40�C to + 7O"C, and shall not suffer damage or deterioration when subjected to storage temperatures in the range - 65�C to + 85�C. 3.2 The switch shall be suitable for mounting through the panel from the rear and shall operate satisfactorily when mounted in any attitude. Other methods of mounting are permissible if specified in the applicable individual specification. .3.3 The switch may be the two or three-position type, with one or more poles; it may be selfretaining and/or spring-return. It shoul-d

arrangement shall be such that wiring access is still proved when the switches are~mounted in rows at minimum spacing.

The switches, when properly installed, shall be suitable for close mounting and shall be constitute an electrical hazard if the side faces of adjacent switches touch one another. 6.7 The switch shall be mounted either: a) by means of a threaded bush, with a locating keyway in the plane of movement of the lever, suitable for use with the panel mounting hole specified in IS 13269 : 1991. Two hexagon mounting nuts, one locating washer and one internal tooth-lock washer shall be provided with each switch; or b) by means of two M4 X 0'7 screws passing through the mounting panel as specified in IS 13269 : 1991. 6.8 The switch shall be so constructed that it is suitable for performing at least 20 000 rated current and operations at maximum voltage. 6.9 The make-and-break of the contacts shall be only that intended by the explicit lever Sprint return switches shall return movement. from their momentary position solely by the internal mechanism of the switch. 7 VOLTAGE 7.1 Voltage The switch shall be nominal 28 V dc. 115/200 V three-phase, addition, the switch voltages down to 4 V 7.2 Current The switch shall be suitable for following nominal current ratings: all of the 4A 15 A 10 A 2A 11 A 7A 2 suitable for operation in 115 V single-phase and 400 Hz ac system. In shall be suitable for use at de or ac. AND CURRENT RATING

referring to ac voltages relate to 315 V with 200 V ( line to line > fclr multi-pole switches, and to 115 V ( phase ) for single-pole switches. All electrical tests shall be performed with the switch connected on each side with cable of a cross-section compatible with the required current. Except for the test in 11.14, each cable shall be 900 & 50 mm in length and shall be attached to the switch using a crimped termination of an approved design. 8.2 Unless otherwise stated, the tests shall be made at a temperature of 15 to 30�C a pressure of 93 to 106 kPa ( 930 to 1 060 m bar ), and at a relative humidity not exceeding 90 percent. 8.3 The cycle of operation for mechanical testing shall consist in movement of the lever from one extreme position of the other and return to the original position. Levers of switches of the spring-return type shall be allowed to return to the biased position without hindrance or assistance from the operating device. The times spent in each position shall be approximately equal. The cycle of operation for electrical tests shall consist of the necessary lever movement to cause one making and one breaking of the contracts under test. 9 DECLARATION

information about the performance of the switch shall be declared in this standard form of declaration as per lS 7855 : 1975. This will include the following: a) classification; b) the limits of the forces necessary to operate the switch to any position; c) the switch operation relative to lever position and terminal numbering; and d) the system of batching used for quality test sampling. 1T) MA-RKING 10.1 The following data shall be marked on each switch in such a position where it can be easily read: a) Indicating the source of manufacture; b) Manufacturer's type No. c) Rated voltage, that is, 28 V/200 V; d) Rated current, for example, `15 A res' ( res = resistive ); e) Batch No., or serial No; and f) Country of manufacturer. 10.2 The switches Standard Mark. may also marked with the

IS 13296 : 1992 11 TESTS 11.1 Type Tests The following shall constitute the type tests : a) b) c) d) e) Visual examination ( see 11.4 >, Dimensions ( see 4.1 ), High voltage test ( see 11.5 >, Insulation resistance test ( see 11.6 ), Voltage drop test ( see 11.7 >, Operating forces test ( see Ii.8 ), Mechanical strength test ( see 11 9 ), Temperature rise test ( see 11.10 ), Mechanical endurance test ( see 11.11), Electrical endurance test ( see 11.12 ), Overload test ( see 11.13 ), Short circuit test ( see 11.14 ), Thermal cycling test ( see 11.15 ), Environmental test ( see 11.16 ), Strip examination and report ( see 11.17 ). 11.5 High Voltage Test A test voltage of 1 500 V rms at 50 Hz shall be applied for a period of not less than 5 seconds between: a) each terminal and all others not connected to it with the lever in each position; and b) all terminals connected together and the metal mounting plate and any exposed metallic parts with the lever in each position. During the test, the voltage shall be increased and decreased gradually 11.6 Insulation Resistance Test Immediately after the high voltage test, the insulation resistance shall be measured at a potential of 500 V dc between the points specified in 11.5 (a) and (b) and shall not be less than 100 M. 11.7 Voltage Drop Test A current of 15A dc shall be passed through the contacts at a suitable voltage. The voltage drop across the switch terminals shall be measured and shall not exceed 100 mV. 11.8 Operating The following tests: shall constitute the acceptance Forces Test

11.1.1 The tests specified in 11.1 (a) to (f) shall be carried out on the same switch. A separate switch shall be used for each of the test specified in 11.1 (g) to (r). 11.2 Acceptance Test

a) Visual examination, b) Dimensions, c) High voltage test, d) Insulation resistance test, e) Voltage drop test, f ) Operating forces test, g) Mechanical strength test, h) Temperature rise test, and j ) Overload test. 11.2.1 A recommended given in Annex A. 11.3 Routine Tests The following shall constitute the ro_utine tests: a) Visual examination, b) Dimensions, c) High voltage test, d) Insulation resistance test, and e) Voltage drop test. 11.4 Visual Examination The switch requirements workmanship shall be examined for the of 6 and 10. The quality/ shall be visaully inspected. scheme of sampling is

The forces necessary for the operation of the switch to all operating positions shall be determined. The force shall be applied at 3 mm from the tip of the lever and at right angles to the lever axis. The test shall be repeated three times in each lever direction. The forces to operate and, if appropriate, to unlock the lever shall Abewithin the declared limits. 11.9 Mechanical Strength Test

11.9.1 Strength of Terminals All terminals shall be separately not less than one minute to: subjected for

a) a pull of 45 N in each of the following directions: parallel to the long axis of the terminal screw or terminal junction

at right angles to the long axis of the terminal screw or terminal junction ( no one terminal shall be tested in more than one direction ); and b) a torque of 1'8 N.m. terminal screw. 11.9.2 Strength of Lever A force of 90 N load shall be applied for not less than one minute to the lever under each of the following conditions, during which the 3 applied to the

IS 13296 : 1992 switch shall be connected electrically to check contact operation: a) perpendicular to the lever axis and parallel to the line of lever travel at each end-position of the lever: b) perpendicular to the lever axis and perpcdicular to the line of travel in both directions throughout the entire range of lever travel; c) coaxial with the lever axis toward and away from the switch body throughout the entire range of lever travel; and d) for locked lever switches, perpendicular to the lever axis in the plane of travel and in the direction to cause operation. The lever shall remain in the locked position. -For the tests in (a), (b) and (c) the load shall be applied 3 mm from the tip of the lever. 11.9.3 Strength of Panel Mounting Bush
A tightening torque of 2'9 N.m. shall be applied for not less than one minute, to the mounting nut with the switch mounting in a panel and located by means of the locating washer and keyway.

11.11 Mechanical endurance Test 11.11.1 Two switches shall be subjected to 40 000 cycles of no-load operation as follows, at a rate of operation between 10 to 18 cycles per minute: a) 30 000 cycles at + 20 f 5�C b) 5 000 cycles at + 70 f 2�C c) 5 000 cycles at - 40 f 2�C
NOTE - For spring-return switches, return from the momentarily actuated position is to be accomplished solely by the internal mechanism of the switch without hindrance or assistance by the operating device. When testing other types, the operating device is not to impart a load to the switch lever in any fixed position of the lever. Following these tests, the switehes shall satisfy the requirements of the voltage drop and insulation resistance tests specified in 11.6 and there shall be no mechanical breakage, malfunction, or deierioration of the switch, when tested in accordance with 11.8 and 11.9. 11.12 Electrical Eodnrance

Test

11.9.4 Requirements The switch shall not be damaged or distorted as a result of the tests in 11.9.1 to -11.9.3, immediately following which it shall: a) satisfy the resistance b) perform operation requirements of the insulation test ( see 11.6 >; and satisfactorily 10 cycles of at 28 V dc resistive load.

11.12.1 Two separate switches shall be subjected to each electrical load rating specified in 7 for 20 000 cycles of operation as follows at a rate between 10 and 18 cycles per minute: a) 10 000 cycles at sea level; b) 9 500 cycles at a pressure corresponding to an altitude of 11 000 m; and c) 500 cycles at a pressure corresponding to an altitude of 20 000 m. 11.12.2 Two switches shall each be subjected to 40 000 cycles of operation as follows at the rate specified in 11.12.1, carrying a 100 mA resistive load at 2 to 4 V dc; a) 20 000 cycles at sea levels; and b) 20 000 cycles at a pressure corresponding to an altitude of 6 100 m. 11.12.3 Following the tests in 11.12.1 the switches shall be subjected to the temperature rise test specified in 11.10. There shsll be no mechanical breakage or damage to the switch mechanism and the switches shall meet the requirements of 11.20. 11.13 Overload Test

11.10 Temperature Rise 11.10.1 The switch, suspended in still air, shall carry the electrical test current until steady conditions are reached. The temperature or temperature rise of any external part of the switch shall not exceed the figures stated in 11.10.2 and 11.10,3. The temperature rise in the attached
cable ( measured with a suitable thermocouple at the surface of the conductor beneath the insulation at a point 25 mm from the end of insulation ) shall not exceed 55�C. For multipole switches the temperature shall be measured with all normally closed poles carrying rated current. 11.10.2 The temperature of any component part of the switch which may normally be -accessible to, or inadvertently touched by, occupants of the aircraft under operating conditions shall not exceed 100�C at maximum ambient temperature. 11.10.3 The temperature rise of any part which is necessarily handled and which is made from a poor or covered with, material which is thermal conductor shall not exceed 20�C. If such a part is made from metal, the temperature rise shall not exceed 10�C. 4

11.13.1 The switch shall be subjected to 50 cycles of operation at the appropriate rate specified in 11.12.1 controlling 150 percent resistive current at 28 V dc. 11.13.2 The switch shall be subjected 50 cycles of operation at the appropriate specified in 11.12.1 controlling 150 percent tive current at 115/200 V ac. 11.14 Short Circuit Test to rate resis-

11.14.1 Switches shall be subjected to the short-circuit test in a following circuit equivalent to that shown in the Fig. 1. The

SIZE 16, COPPER-CORED CABLE, LENGTH 300mm FOR SHORT CIRCUIT TEST

FIG. 1 TYPICAL TEST CIRCUIT circuit shall be adjusted to provide a current of 60 times the rated resistive current at 28 V dc with the selector switch in the calibrate position. For three-position switches, a separate switch may be used for testing each operating position. 11.14.2 The switch under test shall be inserted in the test circuit with its contacts closed, the selector switch set to test, and the circuitbreaker closed. The control switch shall then be closed to initiate the fault current and held closed until the circuit-breaker clears the fault. The fault current shall be applied five times with a minimum interval of 2 minutes between each test. The contacts shall not weld or stick and there shall be no mechanical damage to the switch. After the test the voltage drop across the contracts shall be measured in accordance ,with 11.7 and shall not exceed 2'5 mV. 11.15 Thermal Cycling Test This test is designed to determine the ability `of switches to withstand extremes of high and low temperature and the shock of alternate ~exposure to~those extremes. Separate chambers shall be used for the high and low -temperatures. A cycle shall consist in the switch being placed in the low temperature chamber for 1 h at - 65"C, exposure to normal ambient temperature of 25�C for not more than 5 minutes, exposure in the high temperature chamber for 1 h at + lOO"C, and exposure to normal ambient temperature of 25�C for not more than 5 minutes. .The switch shall be subjected to 3 cycles after which it shah be examined for mechanical and .eletrical damage and ability to conduct current.

There shall be no damage and the switch be conductive at 4 V. 11.16 Environmental Tests 11.16.1 The switches shall meet the ments of the following: Vibration, a>
